transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… it’s mostly that I can’t keep my words in a straight line anymore. I’ll start talking about an overnight shift, and then somehow I’m on soccer, or paint colors, or patient charts, and people just look lost.
Can you explain what happens when your thoughts jump from one topic to another? Do they feel connected to you, or do they feel foreign or confusing?

It feels connected when I’m saying it, I think. Like… the overnight shift makes me think of one thing, then soccer, then paint colors, then charts. But out loud it doesn’t come out straight, and people get lost. I can see it on their faces.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, or that your thoughts are being taken out or broadcasted to others?
I don’t… I don’t think so. I mean, my thoughts get messy, but I haven’t really noticed them being put there by someone else or taken out. Broadcasted… I’m not sure what that would even feel like.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that others don’t seem to hear?
I… don’t think so. Not voices, no. Sometimes I’m not sure if I heard something or if I’m just tired, but nothing I can really say for sure.
Have you ever had experiences where you believed something strongly that others didn’t seem to understand or agreed with, even though you felt it was obviously true?

Yeah… I guess. At work, I’m pretty sure the supervisors changed my shifts on purpose. And… I think they watch me on the unit cameras to see if I’m unsafe.

People keep saying it’s just staffing shortages, but it doesn’t feel like that to me. It seems obvious.
Can you tell me more about why you think the supervisors are watching you on the cameras? Have you noticed any specific behaviors or actions from them that make you feel this way?

It’s just… the timing. My shifts get changed in ways that don’t make sense, and then I notice them looking up at the cameras or acting different around me.

They say it’s staffing, but I don’t really buy that. It feels like they’re checking if I’m going to do something unsafe or mess up. I can’t prove it, but… I’m pretty sure.
Do you ever feel like things happening around you, like TV shows, conversations, or events, are specifically directed at you or have a special meaning for you?

Not really with TV or anything. It’s more… at work. Like the shift changes and the cameras. It feels like that’s about me, like they’re watching to see if I’m unsafe, even though people keep saying it’s just staffing.
Outside of work, do you ever feel like things happening around you, like people's actions or events, are specifically related to you or have a special meaning for you?

Not really… not outside work. It’s mainly the supervisors and the cameras there. The shift changes feel like they’re about me, like they’re checking if I’m unsafe. People say it’s staffing, but… I don’t think that’s all it is.

Even though others have told you that the shift changes are due to staffing issues, do you still feel certain that it's really about being watched or being unsafe, and do you feel that your belief in this doesn't change, even when people try to reassure you?

Yeah… I mean, people keep saying it’s just staffing, but I don’t really believe that.

It feels like they changed my shifts on purpose, and they watch me on the cameras to see if I’m unsafe or something. Reassuring me doesn’t really change it. I’m pretty sure that’s what’s going on.

Even though people have given you explanations like staffing shortages for the shift changes, do you feel completely certain that the real reason is that you’re being watched because they think you might be unsafe?

Yeah… I’m pretty sure. I know they say it’s staffing, but it doesn’t feel like that’s the real reason. It feels like the supervisors changed things and watch me on the cameras because they think I might be unsafe.

Can you tell me if your belief that the supervisors changed your shifts and are watching you on cameras is something you feel absolutely certain about, and has this belief remained unchanged over time, even in the face of other possible explanations?

Yeah… I’d say I’m sure. I know people keep saying it’s staffing shortages, but that doesn’t change it for me. It’s been the same feeling—that they changed my shifts and watch me on the unit cameras to see if I’m unsafe.
Has your belief that the supervisors changed your shifts and are watching you on cameras stayed the same even when there’s no new evidence supporting it, or has it ever changed or wavered at all?

It’s… stayed the same. I know there isn’t always new proof or anything, but I still feel sure they changed my shifts and watch me on the cameras because they think I’m unsafe. Reassurance doesn’t really change it.

Has your belief that the supervisors changed your shifts and are watching you on cameras ever felt completely unshakable, like no amount of reasoning or new information could change it, even if you wanted to consider other explanations?

Yeah… it feels pretty unshakable. I can hear what people say about staffing shortages, but it doesn’t really change it for me. I’m sure they changed my shifts and watch me on the cameras because they think I’m unsafe.

Has this belief that the supervisors changed your shifts and are watching you ever felt so completely true to you that you couldn’t even imagine it being wrong, even if others tried to show you different reasons?

Yeah… I mean, it feels true. Like, I can’t really picture it being anything else. People say it’s staffing, but I’m sure they changed my shifts and watch me on the cameras because they think I’m unsafe.
